title: Archana Puran Singh Adopts Strict Ayurvedic Routine After 15-Day Bengaluru Retreat
excerpt: The 63-year-old actor and Kapil Show regular has cut sugar, maida, and fried food from her diet, now eats dinner at 7 PM and sleeps by 10 PM after completing an Ayurvedic wellness programme.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Archana Puran Singh, 63, adopted a strict Ayurvedic routine after a 15-day retreat in Bengaluru.
  • Her new diet excludes sugar, maida, and fried foods, with dinner at 7 PM and bedtime by 10 PM.
  • Singh shared her meals on social media, highlighting rice-flour momos as a healthy snack option.
  • Experts endorse her diet for promoting gut health and aligning with Ayurvedic principles of digestion.

Actor Archana Puran Singh has returned from a 15-day Ayurvedic wellness retreat in Bengaluru with a transformed daily routine. The 63-year-old, best known as the permanent guest on The Great Indian Kapil Show on Netflix, disclosed the strict regimen she now follows in a vlog on her elder son Aaryamann Sethi's YouTube channel.

The prescribed routine is austere by Bollywood standards: no sugar, no refined flour (maida), no fried food, dinner by 7 PM, and lights out between 10 and 11 PM.

"Mera sab bandh hai. No meetha. No maida. No fried. Sleep at 10 pm–11 pm. No enjoyment. I have to eat dinner at 7 pm."

— Archana Puran Singh, actor

What the Retreat Involved

Singh spent 15 days at an Ayurvedic wellness centre in Bengaluru, undergoing what appears to be a structured panchakarma-style programme — the traditional detoxification and rejuvenation protocol central to Ayurvedic medicine. While she did not name the facility, she shared glimpses of her stay, including views from her room and simple meals prepared according to Ayurvedic dietary guidelines.

On Instagram Stories, she posted her evening snack — rice-flour momos filled with soya — calling them a satisfying alternative to heavier fare. In another story, she showed her morning meal, both consistent with the Ayurvedic emphasis on light, warm, easily digestible food.

"The comedic actor — known for her exuberant on-screen presence — described the routine with self-deprecating humour, joking about the lack of "enjoyment" in her new life."

The retreat also appears to have prescribed a rigid daily schedule. Early sleep, early meals, and the elimination of processed ingredients are all standard components of Ayurvedic dinacharya — the traditional daily routine designed to align the body with natural circadian rhythms, according to Hauterrfly.

Expert Take on the Diet

Singh's food choices drew attention from nutritionists. Dr. Amreen Sheikh, Chief Dietitian at KIMS Hospitals in Thane, told JuszNews that snacks made from rice flour are a sound evening option because they are light and easy to digest — an advantage as the body's digestive capacity naturally slows toward night.

Dr. Sheikh noted that rice is a simple carbohydrate offering quick energy, but warned that rice-flour snacks alone may not sustain fullness. Pairing them with protein or healthy fats — such as vegetable or nut-based accompaniments — can improve satiety and help manage blood sugar levels.

From an Ayurvedic standpoint, rice-flour preparations cooked with minimal oil and spices align well with the tradition's focus on supporting, rather than overloading, evening digestion.

A Wider Wellness Turn in Bollywood

Singh's public embrace of Ayurveda fits a growing pattern among Indian celebrities turning to traditional wellness systems. Actors, cricketers, and business figures have increasingly spoken about panchakarma retreats, Ayurvedic diets, and yoga-based health regimens in recent years. The global Ayurveda market is projected to expand significantly, driven in part by rising interest among India's urban middle class and the diaspora.

What sets Singh's disclosure apart is its candidness. The comedic actor — known for her exuberant on-screen presence — described the routine with self-deprecating humour, joking about the lack of "enjoyment" in her new life. The family vlog format, on a channel run by her son Aaryamann, gave the revelation an unscripted, relatable quality that resonated with viewers.

Diaspora Interest in Ayurvedic Wellness

For Indians living abroad, Singh's experience reflects a broader trend of reconnecting with traditional health practices. Ayurvedic wellness retreats in India have become a draw for NRIs seeking alternatives to Western medical frameworks, with centres in Kerala, Karnataka, and Goa reporting rising bookings from overseas visitors. The appeal is both cultural — a return to ancestral health traditions — and practical, as retreat costs in India remain a fraction of comparable programmes in the West.

Singh's straightforward account of the discipline involved — the early bedtimes, the restricted diet, the sustained commitment — offers a realistic counterpoint to the glamourised portrayal of wellness tourism that often dominates social media.

What's Next

Bollywood's Shift to Ayurveda

Singh continues to appear on The Great Indian Kapil Show, which streams on Netflix. The Sethi family YouTube channel, which crossed one million subscribers earlier this year, recently announced a short break before returning with new content. Aaryamann Sethi's own channel, Aary Vlogs, will continue posting in the interim.

Whether Singh maintains the strict regimen long-term remains to be seen. But for now, the actor who built a career on infectious laughter is betting that going to bed at 10 PM is no joke.
